summary: Round-2 prelaunch re-review of notes/sim10_perlmutter_baseline_20261115 at 296d699. All eight round-1 findings are fixed in code. PM-R1-01: run.sbatch:17 now runs TZ=UTC scontrol. campaign.allocation (campaign.py:33-34) requires 0 < remaining <= 5400+2 s. test_boundaries.py:141-154 covers a Los Angeles process timezone, a mis-encoded local EndTime and an over-long EndTime. PM-R1-02: support.gpu_inventory/normalize_pci builds a normalized UUID-to-PCI map. Campaign requires the inventory to equal the granted UUIDs and passes pci_by_uuid in gpu_plan. runner.py:128 compares the actual CUDA PCI ID with the PCI listed for the assigned UUID, and audit.py:28 repeats the check independently. There are tests for bus-ID formats, duplicate PCI IDs and audit PCI corruption. PM-R1-03: evidence/adapter-port.diff gives the complete adapter edit, including the calibration-source SHA gate. stages.py loads the adapter, and therefore runs the gate, before it loads the same calibration source. PM-R1-04: added tiny-file ECC readback and corruption tests (manifest, size, shape, dtype, pixels, empty bin, counts), which also show that production rejects non-full shapes. Also added affinity prefix/SMT/overlap/outside-mask tests, cache allowlist rejection, bundle file/manifest/external/plan tamper tests and step-timeout kill. PM-R1-05: host_checks.py records the git HEAD, working status and every bundled file type. The supplied exact-commit receipt shows HEAD 296d699 with a clean task tree: 90 passed plus 64 subtests. PM-R1-06: the lock is now taken inside the failure-status handler. PM-R1-07: prepare.py pins PACKAGE/calibration/manifest.json, and load_constants hashes each array against it. PM-R1-08: PLAN states the budget basis and accepts the timeout risk. The reference probe now runs before acceptance, and setup/conditioning progress receipts are written. The coordinator's missing-expand-oracle fix is correct: load_guards AST-extracts the unchanged verify.expand, then device_guards, into a namespace that supplies np, adapter, require, WORDS and PIXELS. I found no blocking regressions. One low, non-blocking provenance gap remains: runner.py has post-port edits (PCI normalization and gate, progress receipts) that neither port_sources.py nor an evidence diff records. This pass covers prelaunch readiness only. GPU execution, the full-shape memory fit, full reference cost, runtime results and an independent review of bundle preparation are all still pending; none is claimed.
